newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-ICI warns govt on rampaging pound.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ICI warns govt on rampaging pound.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc added to a chorus of voices warning of the impact of the rocketing pound on British business on Thursday, after sterling wiped 90 million pounds ($151 million) off its first-half profits.

And ICI, whose half-year profits slumped to 160 million pounds from 367 million on sales down 6.2 percent at 4.97 billion, said full-year profits could be dented by 150 million pounds if sterling remained at current levels.

The company, which is in the process of transforming itself into a major player in speciality chemicals like food flavourings and adhesives, also blamed a continued plunge in prices for bulk chemicals for its disappointing performance.
The worst offenders, titanium dioxide and polyester operations, were largely sold to U.S. rival DuPont & Co last week in a surprise $3 billion deal.
But while ICI told Reuters there were signs chemical prices had reached the bottom of the cycle, they said sterling's rise above three marks was hurting exports and damaging its British customers.

"We think there is evidence now that (supports) the concerns about a strong pound and its impact on exports. It is affecting not only how our businesses do but also affecting our customer base in the UK," chief financial officer Alan Spall said.
He said the pound, which was trading above 3.07 marks on Thursday, "was well overvalued above three marks. We'd be much more comfortable in the 2.50 to 2.60 mark area."

ICI's sales volumes in Britain dropped by five percent in the second quarter, and were down two percent in the first six months of the year. In contrast, sales in mainland Europe rose by nine percent and in the Americas by seven percent.

ICI's comments were underlined by figures from the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) on Thursday showing manufacturers' export orders in the four months to July fell at the fastest rate since October 1991, the middle of the last recession here.
And on Wednesday, British Steel Plc said the pound was "seriously impairing the competitiveness of many of our UK customers."

ICI's results were something of anti-climax after a flood of announcements on its move away from bulk chemicals. The headline figure was flagged last week when it announced the sale of half its bulk chemical operations to DuPont. The dividend was left unchanged at 12 1/2 pence.

ICI shares, which have performed strongly since it announced the acquisition of Unilever Plc's speciality chemical business for $8 billion in May, slipped back 14 1/2 pence to 910 1/2 after touching an all-time high of 944 pence on Wednesday.

The results reinforced its decision to get out of bulk chemicals and concentrate on higher margin businesses like paints, adhesives and acrylics. It is still looking for buyers for its remaining bulk activities.
Spall told Reuters that in a year's time the new-look ICI would be much less vulnerable to cyclical swings and the impact of the pound.
"We are confident we can grow ICI and end up very much stronger," he said. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
